newsitem.title: USA: SangStat says drug is equivalent of Neoral.
newsitem.headline: SangStat says drug is equivalent of Neoral.

text.p: SangStat Medical Corp on Monday said recent tests show its formula for cyclosporine has been found to be bioequivalent to Neoral, a cyclosporine drug being sold by Sandoz AG.

Under current U.S. Food and Drug Administration regulations, a bioequivalent -- or generic -- form of Neoral can be approved without the need to duplicate safety and efficacy trials, according to SangStat.
SangStat filed for approval of its cyclosporine-based drug in November, the company said in a statement.
SangStat shares rose 4-1/2 to 32-7/8 by mid-afternoon.

Cyclosporine is an immunosuppressive drug used in human organ transplantation to prevent graft rejection by the host body. Worldwide sales of Sandoz's cyclosporine total $1.2 billion, according to SangStat.

It said Eli Lilly and Co, which made the batches of cyclosporine used in the bioequivalency trials, also will manufacture SangStat's cyclosporine if it is eventually approved for sale. SangStat will sell and distribute the drug.
Separately, the company also said it has filed a product license application with the FDA for the approval of its drug Thymoglobulin, which also is used to prevent graft rejection.
